whatChanged.theMeasuredDefect: JDF-641's choice widgets 9B.0 (Did you appeal any of these cases), 9B.2 (Appellate Court) and 9C.0 (Do you still owe restitution) on packet page 4 are participant elections the packet deliberately leaves unmade. Read first hand from the pinned binary: all three are /FT /Ch, all three carry /MK /BC [0 0 0], all three ship their own /AP /N stream, and all three hang BELOW an AcroForm root -- the form's /Fields array holds 53 entries against 113 fields, and none of the three is one of them. restrictWidgetContributions dispositions an unwritten chooser as RENDER_PARTICIPANT_VALUE_ONLY_WHEN_WRITTEN and drops it: it clears /AP and removes the /Annots entry, but detachFromAcroForm's flat scan finds the field nowhere in /Fields and walkFieldTree is off, so the field survives in the form. form.updateFieldAppearances() then regenerates an appearance for it -- PDFDropdown.needsAppearancesUpdate returns true because /AP is gone -- and pdf-lib's default provider strokes a rectangle the size of the widget from /MK /BC. flatten() finds the page through the widget's own /P and stamps it.
whatChanged.theSpecification: ISO 32000-1 12.5.6.19 makes /MK /BC and /MK /BG appearance CHARACTERISTICS, consulted only where a viewer must construct an appearance for itself. A widget drawn from its own /AP /N never has its /MK read. The rectangle is therefore produced by the normalization and is on the page only because the normalization ran.
whatChanged.theSharedModule: rcap-active-content.mjs gains ONE opt-in option on sanitizeAndFlatten, default false, plumbed into restrictWidgetContributions as a sixth argument, plus three module-private helpers: textShowingOperands, operandShowsInk and widgetsWhoseSourceAppearanceIsSilent (which decide whether a source appearance draws a word), and neutralizeSynthesizedBorderCharacteristics (which removes /MK /BC and /MK /BG).
whatChanged.theMechanism: Two halves of one remedy, both reached ONLY for a field this run did not write, and both running before any appearance is generated. (1) PRESERVE. Where every widget of an unwritten chooser ships an /AP /N stream that draws no word, that stream is kept instead of cleared, so pdf-lib reports no update is needed and regenerates nothing; the court's own rule is flattened, which is what a conforming viewer paints from the same binary. (2) NEUTRALISE. /MK /BC and /MK /BG are removed from every unwritten field's widgets, so anything still regenerated for one paints no rectangle. The first half is what the measurement supports for this family -- all three widgets ship a usable /AP -- and the second is what covers a widget whose source ships none.
whatChanged.howSILENTIsDecided: Structurally, from the stream's own bytes: it is silent when it contains no text-showing operator (Tj, TJ, ' or ") carrying a character a reader would see. 9B.2's 29-byte appearance is '0 G / 0 0.5 m / 217.8954 0.5 l / s' -- a rule and nothing else. 9B.0's and 9C.0's add a clipped text run whose only operand is '( )', a single space. A stream that DOES show a word is exactly the chooser prompt, default or option list the unwritten-input drop exists to remove, so it is not silent, is not kept, and the drop proceeds unchanged. Every case this cannot read for certain -- a state dictionary, an appearance that is not an indirect stream, an undecodable stream, a text operator whose operand did not parse -- is reported as not silent, because refusing to keep is the answer the pipeline already gives.

A widget the source marks Hidden or NoView, which is dropped before any disposition is read. A chooser whose own appearance shows a prompt.
